title: National Minimum Wage 2026: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Tax and Super
description: Use the national minimum wage 2026 to convert hourly pay to annual salary. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and fortnightly breakdowns for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: At the national minimum wage 2026 of $26.44 per hour, a full‑time worker on 38 hours per week earns about $52,255 per year before tax.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. The national minimum wage 2026 of $26.44 per hour works out to $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,255 per year.

faqs.q: Does the annual figure include superannuation?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% for 2026–27, but it is not part of your annual salary. For example, if your annual ordinary earnings are $52,255, your employer must pay an additional $6,270.60 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

faqs.q: How does tax and the Medicare levy affect my take‑home pay?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates apply: no tax on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the national minimum wage 2026 annual figure of $52,255, the estimated tax is $5,291.25 plus Medicare levy of $1,045.10, leaving about $45,918.65 after tax and Medicare (before any offsets or surcharges).

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary in Australia

If you earn an hourly wage or have been offered a salary, understanding the annual equivalent helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard method is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. For most full‑time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This article uses the **national minimum wage 2026** as a key reference, but the same formula applies to any hourly rate.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

If you work 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52.

For the **national minimum wage 2026** of $26.44 per hour, that gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,255 per year (before tax and super).

If you work a different number of hours each week, adjust the hours figure accordingly. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether to add casual loading. It uses the same 38‑hour assumption unless you change it.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the national minimum wage 2026:

- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90 (the Fair Work Commission figure).
- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80.

This can help you match your pay cycle when budgeting.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates and Casual Loading

The **national minimum wage 2026** is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many workers are covered by industry or occupation awards, which often set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes award pay guides that list specific rates for each classification. The figure of $26.44 per hour is the base rate for a permanent employee.

Casual employees receive a loading of 25% on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the national minimum wage 2026, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it automatically.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. For 2026–27, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual ordinary earnings are $52,255, your employer must contribute an extra $6,270.60 to your super fund. Super is not part of your salary; it is an additional benefit.

### Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your gross annual figure, you can estimate your take‑home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The Australian Taxation Office scales are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For 2026–27, the single reduction thresholds have not been confirmed, so this site uses the 2025–26 thresholds. For most full‑time workers on the national minimum wage 2026, the levy applies at the full 2%.

Example for $52,255:
- Taxable income: $52,255
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 0.15 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $52,255: ($52,255 – $45,000) × 0.30 = $2,176.50
- Total tax: $4,020 + $2,176.50 = $6,196.50
- Medicare levy: $52,255 × 0.02 = $1,045.10
- Total deductions: $7,241.60
- Estimated take‑home pay: $52,255 – $7,241.60 = $45,013.40

Note: This estimate does not include the tax‑free threshold (already applied), the low‑income tax offset, or any other offsets. It also assumes no HELP debt, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice. For a more detailed breakdown, see the [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full‑time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which is about $108,352 per year. All employees (including part‑time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 per year. These are averages across all industries and occupations, not medians for a specific job. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown on this site is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For award‑specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. For more on the national minimum wage, visit the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. If you need to convert a salary to an hourly rate, see the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide.
